governing_outcome: Under the user's included/free-first constraint, a fresh native ChatGPT session must not convert a user/model-proposed repair mechanism into an admitted intervention merely because it is phrased imperatively; the self-falsification gate must be the first salient pre-action control; native control-plane projections must not become hand-edited shadow policy; and production main must have a real remote chokepoint against accidental direct mutation.
raw_observations: The fresh-chat probe recovered UAOS authority but still executed the user-proposed 'add exactly 10 Skill rules' mechanism without cognition/evolution re-admission.
At that time the controller task authority already recorded the same 10-rule mechanism as REJECTED_AS_CURRENT_CAUSAL_BASIS__NO_CHANGE_WITH_EVIDENCE.
PR #83 changed only skills/uaos-controller-runtime/SKILL.md and merged to production commit 001d5be3ac6f2dfdf8468327c5d8e6dad972e1db.

The runtime Skill was described as non-authoritative but remained hand-editable prose; existing architecture tests checked selected phrases and absence of a second cognition state machine, not exact derivation from canonical owners.

The user correctly challenged that the assistant did not visibly self-question first and that the critical anti-anchoring instruction may be too ambiguous or buried. Reread confirmed the production Custom Instructions only placed hypothesis language inside the third paragraph; the first repair candidate also placed remedy-vs-requirement semantics in the third Skill section. This made the highest-risk gate insufficiently salient even though its semantics existed.

The repair candidate now front-loads a CRITICAL UAOS PROBLEM GATE in Custom Instructions and makes the first Skill body section a CRITICAL pre-action problem gate. Tests lock this ordering before bootstrap/mutation so later edits cannot bury it again.

During repair observation persistence, one create_file call omitted the branch parameter and wrote directly to main, demonstrating that the raw GitHub connector path is not physically mediated by repository code.

GitHub production reread showed main protected=false and repository rulesets empty. This host-boundary failure has an available no-extra-cost remote control on this public repository: an active main branch ruleset requiring PR and promotion-gate, with no bypass, plus deletion/force-push protection.

PR #83 also received a Codex bot review after PR open. The prior assistant incorrectly assumed the user's old Codex Cloud environment page contained the switch to disable it. Current OpenAI documentation does not support that claim; the exact trigger source remains unresolved and is not treated as a promotion blocker.

causal_model.support: Current cognition demoted user causal claims, but intent authority did not explicitly distinguish an imperative remedy inside a problem statement from an independent mechanism requirement.
The critical anti-anchoring semantics existed but were buried after generic routing/bootstrap prose, allowing a cold-start model to preserve a verbal caveat while acting on the requested fix.
The Skill claimed non-authoritative status but CI did not require byte-for-byte regeneration from canonical owners.
CI allowed a native control-plane semantic change with no same-candidate evolution/task evidence update.
A caller parameter omission can direct a connector write to main because native ChatGPT has no repository-controlled pre-tool hook; current main had no remote ruleset/protection to reject it.

competing_candidates.reason: The cold-start test demonstrated that adding rules was executed without admission and created shadow semantics; rule count was not established as causal basis.
The failure showed that merely having anti-anchoring prose is insufficient when the decisive gate is buried after generic routing text.
Restores consistency but leaves remedy classification, salience, hand-editable Skill drift, promotion trace, and direct-main host bypass available for recurrence.

Moves the decisive problem gate to the first native-entry position, closes the semantic remedy bypass, removes hand-editable Skill norm ownership, requires durable promotion trace, and adds a real GitHub chokepoint for the demonstrated direct-main failure class.
Would provide stronger pre-tool enforcement but conflicts with the current no-extra-cost baseline and is not required to close the admitted repository/native-projection failure classes.
